newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican daily port, shipping update for Jan 29.
newsitem.headline: Mexican daily port, shipping update for Jan 29.

text.p: Two of Mexico's main crude ports and a total of five ports along the Gulf of Mexico were reported closed Wednesday, the Communications and Transport Ministry said in its 1000 local/1600 GMT daily report.

Crude shipping ports Pajaritos in Veracruz state and Dos Bocas in Tabasco state remained closed Wednesday, port authorities said, as winds at Pajaritos blew at between 70 and 80 km per hour. At Dos Bocas, port officials said winds had relaxed and the port could reopen later in the day.
Other ports shut because of high winds in the regions were Tuxpan in Tamaulipas state, Veracruz in Veracruz state and Campeche in Campeche state.
Smaller ships, such as fishing and tourist boats, were restricted from sailing at ports in Nautla, Alvarado, Altamira, Salina Cruz and Puerto Madero.

The cold front that shut ports in the Gulf of Mexico on Tuesday is expected to gradually extend south toward the Yucatan canal and peninsula. The ministry recommended caution for sailing in the Gulf of Mexico and the Gulf of Tehuantepec because of winds and high waves.
The ministry updated port conditions and shipping warnings for the Gulf of Mexico, Caribbean and Pacific Coast.
Lower temperatures along the western shores of the Baja California peninsula with waves up to 15 feet high. Possible isolated rains in Michoacan state.

In the Golf of Tehuantepec winds were reported from the northeast at 20 to 25 knots (38 to 47 km/22 to 28 miles per hour) with waves from eight to 10 feet high. Winds were expected to relax later in the day. -- Gulf of Mexico:

A moderate cold front heading from the northeast to the south of the gulf, lowering temperatures and bringing north winds of 20 to 25 knots and gusts of up to 45 knots (85 km/50 miles per hour) and waves six to nine feet high.
Cloudy with rains and moderate winds from the north from 20 to 30 km per hour. Violent wind gusts of 80 km reported in the Yucatan canal.
